text:
maya: thinking about a small preflight helper that validates release manifests + runtime signatures before we hand off to deploy-bot. tentative name: sigcheck.

jon: curious — what does sigcheck check that our current preflight doesn't?

maya: quick list: 1) manifest schema diffs (models, routes), 2) artifact sighash verification (KMS/HSM verify), 3) pin-map sanity (no duplicate pins), 4) optional canary routing hints. lightweight so it can run in CI or as a deploy-bot prehook.

leo: nice. can it also produce a rollback stub? e.g. a minimal "rollback-station" plan so on failure we have an automated anchor?

maya: yes — output a tiny yaml: `rollback_plan: { pinned_version: vX.Y.Z, steps: [...] }` and a `rollback-id` that deploy-bot can call.

sam-ci: would like it to integrate as a preflight hook in our pipeline. suggestion: sigcheck exits non-zero on any unexpected manifest change, but can be run with `--allow-minor` to fuzz small non-breaking updates.

maya: sample usage I sketched:
```
# preflight script (ci job)
sigcheck --manifest release.json \ 
         --schema schemas/release-v1.json \ 
         --verify-sig --kms-key projects/prod-kms/key1 \ 
         --out rollback_stub.yaml

if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "sigcheck failed — aborting release"
  exit 1
fi

# continue to enqueue a canary with pin and change window
deploy-bot enqueue --canary --pin-map pin.json --change-window "2026-03-21T02:00Z" --preflight rollback_stub.yaml
```

jon: good. two asks: 1) add a small lint that flags accidental pin collisions, 2) make the change-window human-friendly: allow `cw:fri-2am-UTC` and translate it.

maya: on (1) pin collision lint is cheap — we scan `pin.json` for duplicate targets and overlapping routes. on (2) we can add `--cw-friendly` that expands to an ISO window.

deploy-bot: note: I can accept `--preflight` and store `rollback_stub.yaml` in the release metadata. use `deploy-bot apply --rollback-id <id>` to trigger the rollback-station.

leo: deploy-bot message is perfect. can we also annotate release notes automatically from the manifest diff? a tiny template would help QA and SRE.

maya: draft release-notes template: 
"""
Release: {{version}}
Summary: brief one-line summary
Changes:
- model: {{model_name}} @ {{model_version}} (schema diff: {{diff_summary}})
- infra: {{infra_summary}}
Canary: {{canary_config}}
Rollback ID: {{rollback_id}}
Runbook: link to runbook / incident checklist
"""

sam-ci: if CI can auto-populate that and push to the release ticket, it saves manual copy-paste. add `--notes-out release_notes.md`.

jon: operational thought — watchdog: once canary is live, run a short telemetry probe for 10m and produce an auto-snooze if errors spike. if threshold exceeded, call `deploy-bot apply --rollback-id`. Want that as an opt-in flag `--watchdog auto-rollback`.

maya: agreed. implementation plan:
- v1: sigcheck CLI (go) + pin-collision lint + release-notes template generator (2w)
- v2: deploy-bot preflight flag + store rollback stubs + cw-friendly parser (1w)
- v3: watchdog integration + auto-rollback toggle + CI templates (2w)

leo: scope and owners?

maya: owner: maya (sigcheck + templates), jon (deploy-bot hook + cw parser), sam-ci (CI integration), leo (watchdog + runbook linkage).

sam-ci: I'll add a CI job skeleton in `ci/preflight/sigcheck.yml` and wire `--notes-out`.

jon: can you add a minimal RFC/PR with examples and a quick demo deploy to staging so eng-releases can play with it?

maya: will do — I'll open RFC today and attach a demo video. tagging @jon @leo for review. :rocket:

deploy-bot: reaction saved :thumbsup:

maya: action items: 1) RFC + demo (maya), 2) CI job + job template (sam-ci), 3) deploy-bot hook PR (jon), 4) watchdog probe sketch (leo). I'll drop links in thread once made.

jon: sweet. small step but should reduce manual rollbacks and improve traceability.
